criteria.criterion: The corpus sidecar row preserves `children` as bare ids and persists per-child `children_material` `{canonical_id, title, description}` reconstructed at `review_ts`; a unit test over synthetic child histories asserts CREATE title/description and EDIT title/description updates are reflected as of the parent review timestamp.
`_build_sidecar_row` receives the full per-ticket event store from `_load_ticket_events` and reconstructs each child from the child's own events, not the parent's events.

Rehydrated container cases pass `children_material` title/description records to the finder and G3/G4/decomp-shape are no longer withheld as `container-material-unrecoverable` solely because they are container criteria.

A child whose at-review material is unrecoverable, and any legacy corpus row missing the new `children_material`, withholds that case to drift as unrecoverable rather than calling the finder with an empty/degraded child roster.
The existing protection for non-container criteria and rows with no children is unchanged.

findings.detail: The ticket comment (timestamp 1789014579900794001) describes a live smoke run that found candidate material for G3 (sample_n=5) and G4 (sample_n=5) but failed before model scoring due to a pre-existing runner defect (manifest directory absent, then eval_solver refused agentic filesystem tools). The attestation does not name a specific ledger run ID, ledger entry, or cap value showing the run was recorded in the fixture-admission ledger. The criterion requires the ledger to show the run stayed within the configured cap, but no concrete ledger evidence (run ID, entry, spend amount vs. cap) is cited. The attestation describes a failure before model scoring rather than an explicit ledger/drift no-change outcome within the cap.
findings.remediation: Record a ticket comment or artifact that names: (1) the specific ledger run ID(s) for the G3/G4/decomp-shape admission run, (2) the observed spend amount vs. the configured cap, and (3) either the minted spec path or the explicit drift/no-change ledger entry showing the run completed within the cap.

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: use the evidence path that matches each one. For codebase-verifiable work, complete any unfinished work and make its proof discoverable in the repository. For evidence that inherently lives outside the repository, mark the criterion with the exact `[non-codebase]` tag and add a comment to this ticket that documents the concrete artifacts that meet it (commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the evidence to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so properly tagged evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. An untagged external criterion cannot be satisfied by a ticket comment alone. Then re-verify. Note that a finding reporting a ticket record as absent means it was NOT VISIBLE IN THE TICKET SNAPSHOT THE VERIFIER READ — that snapshot is pinned when the run starts, so a record written after the pin, or not yet committed to the store, reads as missing even though it exists; re-verify after the write lands rather than re-recording evidence you already wrote.
